extraction.Name: Julia Wilson
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her 160 acre allotment at the time it was issued, for she did not want to have the taxes to pay; but that the Indian Agency advised her, if she did not take charge of it, it would be taxed, and finally sold for taxes, so she accepted it
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Charlie Gerber, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $250.00; sold to John Wallace, of Alliance, Nebraska, for delinquent taxes, the mortgage, and $160.00 in cash for her further interest in the allotment
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in taxes, and, in 1920, she mortgaged it to Charlie Gerber; in 1922, she sold it to John Wallace, as she saw she could not make the money good; Wallace paid off the delinquent taxes and the mortgage
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband farms his own place for a living, which constitutes his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health, except for rheumatism; husband has good health; supports her and her five children, all of whom have good health; this makes close living for their family; she considers that she got a very poor price on her land; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document dated December 6, 1928
